latest.text:
Medvedev beat Cobolli in straight sets in Turin, where Cobolli was playing the event for the first time and he needed only two sets to do it.

The first set stayed on serve all the way. Medvedev had five break points in it, early in the set and again at 4–4 but Cobolli saved them all and held each time. Medvedev did not let those missed chances bother him and was too solid in the tiebreak, which he took 7–4 to lead by a set. The second set was tight until he finally broke for 4–3. From there he held and broke once more in the last game, winning 4 games in a row to take the set 6–3 and the match.

Those breaks came late but Medvedev was never in trouble on his own serve. His first serve worked very well and he did not face a single break point all match. On the other side, Cobolli really struggled behind his second serve.

Overall, the gap between the two was clear on a quick indoor hard court that suited Medvedev and a dominance ratio of 1.86 shows how much more he got out of the points than Cobolli. Next is Alcaraz.

latest.text:
Alcaraz beat Tiafoe 6–2, 6–2 in Turin in just 68 minutes, a near perfect display that was strong in every part of his game.

He made a very fast start and broke Tiafoe's serve more than once early in the opening set. Tiafoe had a very hard first six games and never really got back into it, while Alcaraz changed direction easily from cross-court to down the line and sped up in the middle of points to win them. He took the first set 6–2 and was one set away from the win.

It was the same story in the second set. An early break put him in front again and although Tiafoe showed fine touch at times, Alcaraz stayed one step ahead and finished with a dominance ratio of 2.06.

Even the one moment of danger went his way. Tiafoe finally had his chance with 3 break points but Alcaraz saved all of them and held, then broke once more to take the set 6–2 and the match. On the big points he gave nothing away. Next is Medvedev.
